passage:
Thursday, 9:50 pm. Wasim bhai knocked on my door for the third time and asked, "Noor, what happened at school? You barely ate." I stayed on the bed and said nothing. My throat felt like a stone. Something happened with Sana and the group, and I cannot say it aloud yet without crying.
He sat on the floor by the door and did not push. "Okay. I'm not going to make you. But whenever you want to talk, tonight or next week or never, I'm here. No conditions, no questions first."
I said nothing again. But I did not feel alone. I might tell him on Sunday.
— Noor

qa.q: How many times did Wasim bhai knock on the door?
qa.a: Wasim bhai knocked for the third time.

qa.q: What was Noor feeling while staying silent on the bed?
qa.a: Noor felt hurt and unable to say it without crying, with a throat like a stone. The silence protects something painful, not rudeness.

qa.q: What did Wasim do that made Noor feel less alone?
qa.a: Wasim bhai sat on the floor, did not push and said Noor could talk whenever, with no conditions. That gave Noor room to decide.

qa.q: How might Wasim bhai have felt when Noor did not answer?
qa.a: Wasim bhai was probably worried but patient, since he did not press and stayed by the door. Offering to listen later showed care without demand.

grounding: A teenager who says nothing when questioned defends privacy and hides hurt, and is met with an offer to talk later with no conditions.

passage:
Chat, Saturday afternoon
Chetan: Wasim, you've been weird all week. What's going on?
Wasim: nothing
Chetan: Come on, I know something's up. Did I do something?
Chetan: You skipped lunch again too. Just saying.
Wasim: I'm fine. just tired
Chetan: Just tell me, bro.
Wasim: I don't want to talk about it
Chetan: Okay. Sorry for pushing. I'm around if you want. No pressure, even if it's weeks from now.
Wasim: ...
Wasim: not now. maybe later
Chetan: Got it. Cricket tomorrow anyway, come or don't, either way you're in.
Wasim: ok. thanks

qa.q: What did Wasim reply when Chetan first asked what was going on?
What might Wasim have been feeling when writing "I don't want to talk about it"?
qa.a: Wasim was probably hurt and wanting privacy, not ready to explain. The later "not now. maybe later" suggests something painful, and not a refusal forever.

qa.q: What did Chetan do that made it easier for Wasim to reply?
qa.a: Chetan stopped pushing, apologised and said Chetan was around with no pressure, even if it was weeks away. Chetan also kept the cricket invitation open.

qa.q: How might Chetan have felt when Wasim answered "nothing"?
qa.a: Chetan was probably worried and a little hurt, since Chetan kept asking and wondering whether Chetan had done something. Backing off showed care.

grounding: A teenager who says nothing when questioned defends privacy and hides hurt, and a peer offers to talk later with no conditions.
